## pydb\_report Utility

Use the pydb\_report utility with an error database to

- Generate a detailed report of classified errors.
- Regenerate the LAYOUT\_ERRORS file.
- Classify errors.

When an error is classified, the classification tag, UNIX user ID, timestamp, and possible comment are stored with the error in the error database for the current run.

Additionally, the pydb\_report utility can be used on an error classification database to generate a detailed report of classified errors.

## Note:

See Database Naming Conventions on page 318.

<!-- image -->

This utility is in the IC Validator installation bin directory. Table 64 defines the commandline options.

Table 64 pydb\_report Utility Command-Line Options

| Command-Line Option                               | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| -64                                               | Runs the utility with 64-bit coordinates support. This command-line option might be necessary if coordinates in the error database exceed the capacity of a 32-bit signed integer, that is, if the IC Validator tool runs with the -64 command-line option.                                                                                                                                       |
| -classify input_file                              | Classifies errors in an error database based on the given input file. See Classify File Format in the following section.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -classify_by_window [interacting &#124; enclosed] | Specifies how errors are selected for classification based on window coordinates in the classify file. The default is interacting . • interacting . Errors having any interaction with the window coordinates are selected for classification. • enclosed . Errors completely enclosed by the window coordinates are selected for classification. Selected errors can touch the enclosing window. |
| -cpydb_name name                                  | Error classification database (cPYDB) instance name. Required if operating on an error classification database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -cpydb_path path                                  | Error classification database (cPYDB) path. Required if operating on an error classification database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -create_results_report output_file                | Creates a RESULTS-style file from information in the PYDB.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -dlpc <limit>                                     | Limits the error details (coordinates) for each check in the generated LAYOUT_ERRORS or TOP_LAYOUT_ERRORS files to the given number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -help                                             | Displays the usage message.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -le output_file                                   | Generates the LAYOUT_ERRORS file from the current error database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -no_error_details                                 | Does not report error details (that is, coordinates) in the LAYOUT_ERRORS or TOP_LAYOUT_ERRORS files.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -pydb_name name                                   | Error database (PYDB) instance name; usually PYDB_ top_cell . Required if operating on an error database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -pydb_path path                                   | Error database (PYDB) path; usually ./run_details/pydb unless otherwise specified in the db_path argument of the error_options() function. Required if operating on an error database.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Table 64 pydb\_report Utility Command-Line Options (Continued)

| Command-Line Option                                                                              | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| -show_classified [cell= cell ] [violation= comment ] [class= class1 ,..., classn ] [file= file ] | Generates a detailed classified error report for an error database and error classification database. The specified parameters can restrict the report by violation, cell, and class. If the output file is not specified, output goes to the screen.                                                                                                |
| suppress_classified_er rors                                                                      | If specified, no classified errors are reported in the LAYOUT_ERRORS or TOP_LAYOUT_ERRORS file. All classified errors are suppressed, whether they come from the error classification database or an IC Validator option that classifies errors programmatically, or have been classified after the IC Validator run with VUE or the error database. |
| -tle output_file                                                                                 | Generates the TOP_LAYOUT_ERRORS file from the PYDB database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -V                                                                                               | Prints the utility version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -verbose_results_file                                                                            | Controls the output when pydb_report -create_results_report is used.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Classify File Format

The format of the input file for the -classify command-line option is a comma-delimited file with these columns: Cell, Violation, Class, Comment, x1, y1, x2, y2. See Figure 94.

- If a cell is given but not a violation, all errors within the cell are classified.
- If a violation is given but not a cell, all errors within the violation are classified.
- If window coordinates are given, a cell is required and errors that interact with that window are classified. The default is any interaction, but you can change this behavior using the -classify\_by\_window command-line option.

The formatting of records in the file should follow the standard RFC4180 recommended guidelines for CSV files with no column headings. This formatting is supported by Microsoft Excel and other spreadsheet tools.

The classifications you can choose the classifications shown in Table 65.

| Classification   | Description                                 |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Error            | Unclassified error (default classification) |

Table 65 Classify File Format

<!-- image -->

Table 65 Classify File Format (Continued)

| Classification   | Description                                                                                            |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Ignore           | Error that the designer does not care about: to be fixed later in the process flow                     |
| Waive            | Intended design error. It exists at sign-off.                                                          |
| Watch            | Error that needs to be fixed in the next design cycle.                                                 |
| Fixed            | Error that has been fixed in the layout                                                                |
| Unmatched        | Error that exists in an imported error classification database but was not produced by the current run |

## Using Regular Expression Matching

In the input file specified by the -classify command-line option you can now use regular expressions for matching violation comments and cell names in the error database. This matching is enabled by using leading and trailing forward slash (/) characters, with an optional modifier character after the trailing slash. The modifier characters are shown in Table 66

Table 66 Modify Characters for Use in the Classify File

| Modify character   | Description                                |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| m                  | Match case. This character is the default. |
| i                  | Ignore case.                               |

For example, the following line in a classify file results in all violation comments starting with M1, M2, M3, or M4 in cell Cell1 being classified as ignore:

```
Cell1,"/^M[1-4].*/",Ignore,"comment"
```

The following line in a classify file results in violations in all cells containing 'sram', ignoring case, being waived:

```
"/.*sram.*/i","",Waive,"comment"
```

A violation comment that actually begins with a slash cannot be matched with a literal string, but must use GNU extended regular expression special characters. See the table of these special characters in the text\_options() function in the IC Validator Reference Manual for more information. For example, the following in a classify file would match a violation comment containing '/M4 rule 5/':

```
"/\/M4 rule 5\//"
```

<!-- image -->

## Examples

To regenerate TOP.LAYOUT\_ERRORS from the current run, use this syntax:

```
pydb_report -pydb_name PYDB_TOP -pydb_path ./run_details/pydb \ -le TOP.LAYOUT_ERRORS
```

To classify errors in the error database for the current run, use this syntax:

```
pydb_report -pydb_name PYDB_TOP -pydb_path ./run_details/pydb \ -classify classify.csv
```

To show classification details on screen of all ignored and waived errors in the cell TOP, use this syntax:

```
pydb_report -pydb_name PYDB_TOP -pydb_path ./run_details/pydb \ -show_classified cell=TOP class=Ignore,Waive
```

To show classification details of all waived errors in an error classification database, use this syntax:

```
pydb_report -cpydb_name CPYDB_TOP -cpydb_path ./cpydb \ -show_classified class=Waive
```

To use -verbose\_results\_file &lt;value[s]&gt; with -create\_results\_report , use the following syntax:

```
pydb_report -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -verbose_results_file ERRORS,PRE_WAIVED_ERRORS,FLAT_VIOLATION_COUNT,TOTAL_VIOLATION_COUNT,ASSI GNS -create_results_report TOP.report
```

## Note:

You need to enclose &lt;value[s]&gt; in double quotation marks if they contain any whitespace characters.

The verbose\_results\_file argument can have up to five values to control the verbosity of the results file generated by IC Validator. The default is ERRORS . These values are:

- ERRORS . Reports each rule name and the total number of violations for that rule.

## Note:

When using error classification, the number of waived violations is excluded from the number of violations found in the cell .RESULTS file. For example, the tool detects 100 violations, but 60 of them are waived. Therefore, the number of violations reported is 40.

- PRE\_WAIVED\_ERRORS . Specifies the reporting of pre-waiver violation counts in a separate table following the current (post-waiver) violation counts table.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- FLAT\_VIOLATION\_COUNT . Reports the flat violation count for each rule in the error details section and the total flat violation count in the error summary section.
- TOTAL\_VIOLATION\_COUNT . Reports the total number of hierarchical and flat violation counts at the top of the rules table in the error details section.
- ASSIGNS . Reports each assign layer name, hierarchical and flat polygon counts for the layer (or 'Pruned' if the layer was pruned), and additional assignment information for the layer from the assign functions in the runset.

These enum values can be used with the verbose\_results\_file argument in the pydb\_report utility to customize the output in the results file.

Following is a part of the TOP.report file for a small PYDB (after manually waiving one of the two violations belonging to "MyRule").

## Note:

Waived violation counts do not show in this report.

```
... ... - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -Rule                          Violations Found TOTAL                         v = 2 (2) MyRule                        v = 1 (1) Violation                     v = 1 (1) text_net:text_short           v = 1 (1) - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -Rule                          Pre-Waived Violations Found TOTAL                         v_all = 3 (3) MyRule                        v_all = 2 (2) Violation                     v_all = 1 (1) text_net:text_short           v_all = 1 (1)
```

## pydb\_export Utility

Use the pydb\_export utility to export error classification data from an error database to either

- Create a new error classification database (cPYDB). See Error Classification Database Format on page 337.
- Merge into an existing error classification database by appending new errors and updating existing ones.

Also, the pydb\_export utility can be used to manage error classification databases by merging several error classification databases together or by purging classification data from violations and cells.

<!-- image -->

For an error to be considered equivalent between runs, the violation comments must match exactly or match up to the first occurrence of a specified comment delimiter, and the error polygon must match at cell level.

## Note:

See Database Naming Conventions on page 318.

This utility is in the IC Validator installation bin directory. Table 67 defines the commandline options.

Table 67 pydb\_export Utility Command-line Options

| Command-Line Option            | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| -64                            | Runs the utility with 64-bit coordinates support. This command-line option might be necessary if coordinates in the error database exceed the capacity of a 32-bit signed integer, that is, if the IC Validator tool runs with the -64 command-line option.                                                                                                                                                |
| -cell cell                     | Limit exports to errors of the given cell. This command-line option can be given more than one time to specify multiple classes. It supports regular expressions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -class class                   | Limit exports to errors of the given classification. This command-line option can be given more than one time to specify multiple classes. It supports regular expressions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -comment_match_delimiter delim | Match violation comments up to the specified delimiter. When exporting an error database, the default of the delimiter is whatever is specified in the runset using the comment_match_delimiter argument of the error_options() function. When merging multiple error classification databases, however, this command-line option delimiter should be specified to use partial violation comment matching. |
| -convert_to_64                 | Convert a 32-bit or variable width coordinate error classification database (cPYDB) to a 64-bit coordinate error classification database. When used with the -copy_cpydb or -create command-line options, this command-line option converts the database to 64-bits when it is created. Otherwise, it converts an existing database in place.                                                              |

| Command-Line Option                     | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Error Classification Database Format

The error classification database contains classification tags, user IDs, timestamps, comments, and error polygons for the classified errors. When an error classification database is used in a subsequent run, errors that match are annotated in the database with a reference to the error classification database. The actual classification data for these errors remains in the error classification database. Therefore, to view errors for the current run, the error classification database needs to be present in the location specified when the IC Validator tool was run. Also, if data is purged from the error classification database or is overwritten, you cannot view the matched errors from the current run.

<!-- image -->

## Purge File Format

The format of the input file for the -purge command-line option is a comma-delimited file with two columns: Cell and Violation.

- If a cell is specified but not a violation, all errors within the cell are purged.
- If a violation is specified but not a cell, all errors within the violation are purged.

Format the records in the file to follow the standard RFC4180 recommended guidelines for CSV files with no column headings. This formatting is supported by Microsoft Excel and other spreadsheet tools.

## Examples

To create a new error classification database (cPYDB) containing classification data from the current run, use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -pydb_name PYDB_AD4FUL \ -pydb_path ./run_details/pydb \ -cpydb_name CPYDB_AD4FUL -cpydb_path ./cpydb \ -create
```

To set the password on an error classification database, use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -cpydb_name CPYDB_AD4FUL -cpydb_path ./cpydb \ -password oldpassword -set_password newpassword
```

To merge classification data into an existing error classification database that is password protected, use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -pydb_name PYDB_AD4FUL \ -pydb_path ./run_details/pydb \ -cpydb_name CPYDB_AD4FUL -cpydb_path ./cpydb \ -merge -password password
```

To merge several error classification databases together, creating a new error classification database, use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -cpydb_name CPYDB_MY_DESIGN -cpydb_path ./cpydb \ -merge_cpydb name=CPYDB_CELLA path=./cpydb \ -merge_cpydb name=CPYDB_CELLB path=./cpydb \ -merge_cpydb name=CPYDB_TOP path=./cpydb \ -create
```

To convert an error classification database with 32-bit coordinates to one with 64bit coordinates in place, use the following syntax. When using the -convert\_to\_64 command-line option, you need exclusive access to the database; that is, the database cannot be open by VUE, any other scripts, or IC Validator jobs.

```
pydb_export -cpydb_name db name -cpydb_path db path -convert_to_64
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To copy an error classification database and convert it to 64-bit without modifying the original database, use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -cpydb_name db name -cpydb_path db path \ -copy_cpydb name= input db name path= input db path \ -convert_to_64
```

The pydb\_report utility can provide information about the coordinate width of an existing error classification database:

```
pydb_report -cpydb_name CPYDB_AD4FUL64 -cpydb_path ./cpydb ... (C) Copyright 2008-2014. Synopsys, Inc.  All rights reserved. cPYDB Name ............ CPYDB_AD4FUL64 cPYDB Path ............ ./cpydb Coordinate Width ...... 64 bit
```

To export only the classes starting with 'W' in all cells that do not start with "W", use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -class "/^W.*/" -exclude_cell "/^W.*/" ...
```

To export all classes except 'Ignore' and 'Waive', use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -exclude_class Ignore -exclude_class Waive ...
```

To export only the top cell, use this syntax:

```
pydb_export -cell TOP ...
```

## Flattening an Error Classification Database

When an error classification database is generated using block-level IC Validator results, with plans to use it for hierarchical error classification at the chip level after the block is placed, it is advisable to flatten the block-level results if there are any shared sub cells between the current block and other blocks that are placed in the top-level design. The IC Validator tool might push errors down into a sub cell as part of hierarchical DRC checking. If the block-level error classification database is not flattened, it might contain waivers in a shared sub cell that apply only in the context of the block, but are invalid after the block is placed in a larger design with other instances of the shared sub cell. Flattening the block-level error classification database avoids this situation.

The pydb\_export utility flattens an error classification database, using the same layout and top cell which were used in the original IC Validator run that created the violations. The layout must be supplied to provide hierarchy information for the flattening process. Violations in the error classification database are flattened to the provided top cell. Only violations in or hierarchically underneath the provided top cell are output.

<!-- image -->

The layout is specified as a path, using the same convention as the library1 and library2 command-line options of the LVL utility:

```
· GDSII: /path/to/file.gds · OASIS: /path/to/file.oas · Milkyway: /library/path/LIBRARY_NAME · OpenAccess: /path/to/lib.defs/LIBRARY_NAME · NDM: /library/path/LIBRARY_NAME
```

The flattening process can be distributed using the -host\_init command-line option of the pydb\_export utility. The following use cases are supported.

## To flatten during export from PYDB:

```
pydb_export \ -pydb_path path -pydb_name name \ -cpydb_path output_path -cpydb_name output_name \ -create \ -flatten layout= layout cell= topcell \ [-host_init number ]
```

## To copy a cPYDB and flatten the destination cPYDB:

```
pydb_export \ -copy_cpydb path= path name= name \ -cpydb_path output_path -cpydb_name output_name \ -flatten layout= layout cell= topcell \ [-host_init number ]
```

To flatten a cPYDB in place:

```
pydb_export \ -cpydb_path path -cpydb_name name \ -flatten layout= layout cell= topcell \ [-host_init number ]
```

## Using PERC Error Classification

Error classification is supported for netlist-based PERC device and net errors. The overall flow is identical to the flow for DRC error classification. Errors from an initial IC Validator run are classified using VUE or one of the PYDB utilities and are then exported to an error classification database (cPYDB) so that the classifications might be applied in subsequent IC Validator runs. The cPYDB should be specified in the error\_options(match\_errors) argument just as with DRC error classification.

## Note:

Classification is only supported for netlist-based PERC flows and is not available for layout-based flows. Only device and net errors are supported.

## Matching Classified Errors

Netlist-based errors are different from DRC errors in that there are no shapes or coordinates available to uniquely identify particular error instances In addition, netlistbased errors have more metadata associated with them. Here is an example of a device error.

```
Structure Device name（Type) Comment axadoxd/[6e2] (Pin)Pin Net Reference Device （Type) (Pin)Pin Net Reference Instance （Cell Name) Reference Net Name origin net property Merge Member dwc_eusb2 Xu_eusb/XI206/M7 (nch) vdd12->vss;finger width=0.624 [ncs2_enddev] (DRN)Xu eusb/net2366 [ncs2_net] (GATE) Xu_eusb/XI206/vreg (SRC)VSS [ground] (BULK)VSS [ground] vdd12 [power] VSS [ground]
```

In addition to the cell name and device instance and model names, the error instance has a Comment field that can be unique for each error instance, all of its pin names and associated nets, possibly a set of reference objects (cell instances, device instances, nets), whether the device was a result of merging, tags, and so on. Net errors have a similar set of metadata. Errors are matched at the cell level based on the following criteria:

## Device Errors

- Violation Comment / Rule
- Cell Name
- Device Name
- Device Type
- Comment

Net Errors

<!-- image -->

- Violation Comment / Rule
- Cell Name
- Net Name
- Comment

If all of these criteria of a new error match a classified error in the cPYDB, IC Validator applies the classification to the new error.

## Hierarchical PERC Error Classification

IC Validator provides a hierarchical mode that allows classifications from errors that were reported in a lower level of hierarchy to be applied if they are reported at a higher level in a subsequent IC Validator run.

When checking device errors for classification in hierarchical mode, if the device has an instance path, such as the one in the previous example, the device error should be classified if issued at a higher level of hierarchy as long as the original instance name and cell are at the bottom of the new instance path. Nets must match in the same way. The original instance name and cell should be at the bottom of the new instance path.

Classification matches are first attempted at the cell level. If no cell-level match is found, IC Validator looks down the hierarchy to search for a classified error that matches part of the instance path. It is possible that an error might match multiple classified errors. IC Validator applies the first match it finds looking down the hierarchy, and any other potential matches are ignored.

## Hierarchical Example

For this example, refer to the device error from the previous example. It is reported and waived in cell dwc\_eusb2 with device name Xu\_eusb /XI206/M7. If IC Validator is rerun on the same block, it is very likely that an exact cell-level match is found.

If IC Validator is run on higher-level block dwc\_top and the error is reported with device name X1/X2/Xu\_eusb/XI206/M7, then IC Validator searches for a matching classified error as follows:

- IC Validator searches for a cell-level match in dwc\_top, and no matching classified error is found.
- X1 in dwc\_top is an instance of cell dwc\_mid. IC Validator searches for a classified error in cell dwc\_mid with a device name of X2/Xu\_eusb/XI206/M7, and no match is found.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- X2 in dwc\_mid is an instance of cell dwc\_eusb2. IC Validator searches for a waiver in cell dwc\_eusb2 with a device name of Xu\_eusb/XI206/M7. This matches the error from the previous example, so the classification is applied to the error being reported in dwc\_top.

The same methodology is used to hierarchically match net names for net errors.

## 15

## DRC Waivers

This chapter explains the DRC waivers capabilities of the IC Validator tool and how to use this feature.

The DRC waivers capabilities are described in the following sections:

- Defining Waivers
- Creating a Waiver Database
- Using a Waiver Database

DRC waivers allow you to classify and annotate errors found during an IC Validator run and export the errors into a waiver database for use in subsequent IC Validator runs. The DRC Waivers flow is separated into three distinct steps:

- Defining which errors might be waived, and annotating the error database through VUE or the icv\_pydb command-line utility
- Creating a persistent waiver database on disk
- Applying the waivers to subsequent IC Validator runs

Each of these steps is described in the following sections.

<!-- image -->

Figure 96 General Waiver Flow

<!-- image -->

## Defining Waivers

You can review design errors written to the error database (PYDB) using VUE or the ASCII Error Report file, cell . LAYOUT\_ERRORS. In many designs, there are DRC violations that can be waived, that is, these errors do not need to be fixed in the layout. This could be a temporary waiver that must be fixed before the design is taped out, or a permanent waiver that is approved by the foundry. You can add a user comment or predetermined waiver properties to waivers to give more context to other engineers that are reviewing the waivers.

<!-- image -->

The IC Validator SQLite error database allows for concurrent access by multiple users; as errors are reviewed and waivers are applied, other users who access the database can see the updates you have applied.

IC Validator supports several waiver classes:

- Persistent waiver classes: Waive, Watch, Ignore
- Non-Persistent waiver classes: Error, Fixed

Persistent waiver classes can be exported to a waiver database. See Creating a Waiver Database. With multiple persistent waiver classes, you can segregate waived errors into different categories. This makes waiver management easier during the design process. Each of these waiver classes are treated equally. For example, you can choose Waive when the error is waived throughout the design process all the way to tapeout, and choose Watch to designate errors that can be fixed in the next iteration or two of the design.

Non-persistent waiver classes provide information to other users who debug the same error database. For example, with an error defined as Error with the user comment, 'this error needs to be fixed in conjunction with rule ABCD', anyone reviewing the error in the same error database can see this guidance.

<!-- image -->

## Using VUE to Define Waivers

The most common way to define waivers is through the VUE DRC browser. There are several ways to waive errors.

To waive all error shapes in a violation (rule), select the violation in the Violation Browser and right-click to see the menu of options. Choose the appropriate waiver class, as shown in Figure 97.

The Context option determines when these waivers apply as they are used in future IC Validator runs. When set to ALL, the waiver is always applied if matched to an error. When set to the top cell (in this example, the top cell name is 'top') , the waiver is applied only if the current top block is run again as the top cell.

## Defining Waivers Using the Command-Line Utilities

You can define waivers using the icv\_pydb command-line utility. See Error Management Utility for more information.

## Custom Waiver Properties

Along with the user comment, you can define additional waiver properties for a given rule and cell. These properties are useful for adding information and providing additional ways to manage waivers across designs or process node. For example, waivers can be given a waiver property that defines a specific tracking number and its current management approval status. If the waiver is not approved, any waiver with the waiver tracking number can be removed from the waiver database using pydb\_export and the -select\_waiver\_properties command-line option.

<!-- image -->

The allowable values are defined in a JSON format file, which is read by VUE.

Example 42 JSON Property File (waiver\_properties.json)

```
{ "waiver_property_definitions": [ { "property_name": "WaiverTracking#", "property_values": [] }, { "property_name": "Valid_through", "property_values": ["milestone1", "milestone2", "milestone3"] }, { "property_name": "Status", "property_values": ["pending", "approved", "not approved"], "default_value": "pending" } ] }
```

Each property has a property\_name , property\_values, and an optional default\_value. The property\_name follows OASIS property standards, which means it uses printable ASCII characters, excluding spaces, tabs, newlines, and control characters. The property value is not restricted.

## Note:

The WAIVER\_REPORT file uses '|' as a delimiter between multiple property values. To avoid confusion, do not use this character.

VUE reads the JSON file when the following environment variable is set.

```
setenv ICV_WAIVER_PROPERTY_DEFINITION_FILE waiver_properties.json
```

It then creates a custom window with the allowable properties.

In the Violation Browser, right-click to select a rule and cell. The Add Waiver Properties option is now available.

<!-- image -->

## Figure 104 Add Waiver Properties

<!-- image -->

Select this option to define the user properties.

<!-- image -->

All waived errors for the rule/cell inherit the properties. You can see the properties in the Violation Detail pane, as shown here.

<!-- image -->

## Creating a Waiver Database

After you define all of the waivers for the current design, export the information to a standalone waiver database. The waiver database can either be in SQLite format (CPYDB) or OASIS format. The waiver database is self contained. This means that all information required for waiver errors is contained within the database, that is, user comments, user-IDs, dates, waiver properties, and so on.

<!-- image -->

You can export a waiver database using VUE or from the pydb\_export command-line utility.

To export a SQLite waiver database using VUE, select Classification &gt; Export Classification Data (CPYDB).

The output database name is written to the working directory where VUE was started. To write the file to another path, include that path in the output file name. By default, IC Validator creates a new waiver database. You can append this information into an existing CPYDB database by setting the Append Mode. During export, VUE exports any new waivers defined in the error database. To include all waivers, including those that were previously matched from another waiver database, check the Include Matched Errors box. The SQLite format allows you to set a password for the waiver database. This prevents modifying the waiver database unless the password is known.

To export an OASIS format waiver database from VUE, select Classification &gt; Export Classification Data (OASIS).

<!-- image -->

Here you see a window that provides the settings for the waiver database.

<!-- image -->

The output database name is written to the working directory where VUE was started. To write the file to another path, include that path in the output file name. The output OASIS format places waiver shapes in a specially named cell that provides the rule and cell name for each set of waivers (Rule\_Name@cellname). The Rule Name Delimiter allows you to define the delimiter for your process nodes rule names. In the following examples, the rule names use the ':' character as a delimiter between rule name and rule description. When set, all characters to the left of the delimiter define the waiver cell name. If it is not set, or if the rule name is very long, the Max Rule Name Length truncates the waiver cell name to that length. The default is "[[:space:]]+:|[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]", which matches most foundry runset naming conventions.

<!-- image -->

The OASIS format waiver database can now be opened IC Validator WorkBench. In the tree view for the waiver database, as shown the following figure, you can see that the database has a cell with the prefix @. This is a holding cell that contains all of the waivers defined for that cell. This cell does not contain any waiver shapes. Those are contained in the rule-specific cells that are placed within the holding cell.

<!-- image -->

Each waiver cell (rule@cell) has properties attached on the cell.

<!-- image -->

These properties are set during export. The person who exported the waiver database has their user-ID listed in the createID property as well as the timestamp of the export.

The waiverChecksum property is calculated on export for the cell. When IC Validator reads the waiver cell, it calculates a checksum and compares it to the stored property. If the properties are different, this indicates the database has been modified since it was exported. The end of the WAIVER\_REPORT file includes information on whether the check sums match or not.

<!-- image -->

All waiver shapes for a given Violation/Cell are written to an arbitrary layer number. IC Validator does not use the layer number, but rather the violationComment property to know what rule the waiver shapes apply to. Therefore, no mapping file is needed.

## Using a Waiver Database

After you create the waiver database, you can use it as input to other IC Validator runs. The new runs do not have to be the same top cell. IC Validator imports all waiver shapes the Cell / Violation present in the current run. IC Validator waivers are fully hierarchical.

<!-- image -->

The waiver\_options() function provides control over how waivers are applied and reported during the IC Validator run. This command is divided into two main sections. The first section includes database management, where you provide the list of waiver databases and customize how each one is processed. The second section provides global waiver control that IC Validator uses for all waivers and reporting.

The database management is controlled with the databases argument. IC Validator automatically detects the database format, and both CPYDB and OASIS formats can be supplied in the same IC Validator run. Layer mapping files are not required when using OASIS format waiver databases.

For each waiver database, you can customize controls to provide flexibility across designs. This includes:

- Control over what happens if the waiver database cannot be found.
- If the errors waived with this database should be suppressed instead of classified. Suppressed means the waived errors are not written to the PYDB or LAYOUT\_ERRORS file.

<!-- image -->

- Cell prefixes or cell suffixes can also be given for a waiver database. This is useful if you have a flow that uniquifies cells when placed inside of larger macro blocks, but the waivers for the base cell can still apply to the renamed cell.
- Generating a special report that lists all waiver shapes in the database that were not matched during the IC Validator run.

The global waiver controls how waiver shapes are compared to the error shapes found during the run, including any rule-specific overrides and report generations.

## Matching Modes

You can control how IC Validator matches a waiver shape to a given error shape. All matching occurs after all interacting waiver shapes have been merged together and interacting error shapes have been merged together. In some situations, to allow the merging to occur, the shapes might need to be leveled to a common parent cell. The matching is done hierarchically, that is, the level-merged waiver shapes do not need to be in the same cell as the level-merged errors shapes to find a match.

There are three matching modes available: EXACT, ENCLOSE (default) , and INTERACT.

- EXACT mode specifies that the level-merged waiver shape must exactly match the level-merged error shape for the waiver to be applied.
- ENCLOSE mode is the default matching mode. The waiver shape must enclose the error shape.
- INTERACT mode specifies that any error which interacts hierarchically with a waiver shape is waived. Use the include\_touch argument to allow outside-touch interactions to be considered as an interaction for waiving.

## Note:

Use the tolerance argument to provide better matching with all-angle shapes.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The matching mode you set in the waiver\_options() function apply to all waiver\_databases. You can override the matching mode for specific rules using the rule\_overrides argument. For example, ENCLOSE mode is allowed for all rules except R.MY.STRICT\_RULE. For that rule, waivers are applied only if the waiver and error shapes exactly match. For example,

```
waiver_options( databases = { {"/path/to/waiver.oas"}}, matching_mode  = ENCLOSE, rule_overrides = { violation_comments = {"R.MY.STRICT_RULE"}, matching_mode = EXACT, tolerance     = 0.005 } );
```

## Waiver Report File

IC Validator writes all classified (waived) errors to a waiver report file in the IC Validator working directory ( cell .WAIVER\_REPORT).

The LAYOUT\_ERRORS file and VUE run\_summary tab state

```
ERRORS (WAIVERS APPLIED)
```

The waiver report file is generated by default with a summary of rules, including applied waivers and a list of input waiver databases.

```
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------WAIVER SUMMARY -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

<!-- image -->

```
R.M3.L: M3 cannot have 3 or mor... | Waive : 5 | Ignore : 0 | Watch : 0 | WaiverConflict : 0 | Unmatched : 0 R.M4.W: M4 Minimum width >= 0.24    | Waive : 4 | Ignore : 0 | Watch : 0 | WaiverConflict : 0 | Unmatched : 0
```

The table columns are: Rule name, Waive, Ignore, Watch Class counts, WaiverConflict count, and Unmatched waiver counts.

- A waiver conflict occurs when interacting waiver shapes with different waiver classes are level-merged together.
- Unmatched is a count of waiver shapes for the rule across all input waiver database that did not have a match in the current design.

IC Validator can also generate a detailed waiver report by setting

```
waiver_options(report_waiver_details = true)
```

This adds a table for every waiver, the cell, waiver class, matching mode, context, the waiver database with the waiver shape that matched, any waiver properties, and error details (distance, bounding box, and so on).

## Note:

```
The waiver_options() function can be modified by using the -runset_config command-line option.
```

You can generate the waiver report file after an IC Validator run completes. This can be useful if you do not want to view the details that are on by default in your IC Validator runs, but want to see them after the run.

```
%icv_pydb -i ./run_details/pydb/PYDB_top \ -create_waiver_report top.DETAILED_WAIVERS \ -include_waiver_details
```

A JSON-formatted version of the waiver report file can also generated using the icv\_pydb utility. If you need to write a script to process the waivers applied on a given design, this structured format is an easier file to parse.

```
% icv_pydb -i ./run_details/pydb/PYDB_top \ -create_json_waiver_file top.waiver_file \ -include_waiver_details
```

Example 43 JSON Format Waiver Report File

```
{ "icv_run_info": { "library_name": "../../../lab_data/INLIB_TRAINING.GDS", "structure_name": "top", "generated_by": "IC Validator RHEL64 S-2021.06-SP3-BETA-20211123.7086978 2021/11/23", "runset_name": "../modular.rs",
```

<!-- image -->

## 16

## Error Management Utility

This chapter explains the error management utility that is available with the IC Validator tool.

The error management utility is described in the following sections:

- Error Management Utility
- Splitting Error Databases
- Merging Error Databases
- Applying Waivers to an Existing Error Database
- VUE File Support
- Modifying Databases in Place
- Hierarchy Considerations
- XML Command File
- Exporting Errors to a Layout
- Managing Referenced cPYDB Paths

## Error Management Utility

Use the error management utility (icv\_pydb) to

- Split an error database (PYDB) from a single IC Validator run into multiple databases for debugging purposes.
- Select errors from an input PYDB and create a new PYDB with only the selected errors.
- Merge multiple PYDB databases together.
- Alter an existing PYDB database by renaming violations or cells, or classifying errors.

<!-- image -->

- Export errors in a PYDB database to a layout.
- Group DRC errors.

The icv\_pydb utility provides command-line options to enable any selection by cell (either individually or hierarchically), violation comment,violation name, error classification, or celllevel bounding box.

This utility is in the IC Validator installation bin directory. Table 68 defines the commandline options.

## DRC Error Grouping

The error database management utility can be used to place DRC errors into groups that have the same violation marker shape and properties. The error grouping can be used in VUE to display only a representative error from each group using the Show Unique and Highlight Unique menu options. By default, the grouping is done regardless of orientation. For example:

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOPCELL -group_drc_errors
```

See Table 68 for information on the error management utility command-line options.

<!-- image -->

## Splitting Error Databases

If there are multiple blocks in a design,

<!-- image -->

A   B     A  C     B   D

The results might be split into three error databases PYDBs), one for each subblock. For example:

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical "Block1"\ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block1 -vue Block1.vue -vue_template TOP.vue icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical "Block2"\ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block2 -vue Block2.vue -vue_template TOP.vue icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical "Block3"\ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block1 -vue Block3.vue -vue_template TOP.vue
```

Use the -select\_cell\_hierarchical command-line option to automatically pull in any descendant cells placed underneath the selected cells. In this example, the commandline options pull in A and B under Block1, A and C under Block2, and B and D under Block3. Cells can be included or excluded individually without including subtrees using the -select\_cell or -unselect\_cell command-line options. Alternatively, this operation can be specified by a single icv\_pydb command:

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical "Block1"\ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block1 -vue Block1.vue -vue_template TOP.vue \ -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical "Block2" \ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block2 -vue Block2.vue -vue_template TOP.vue \ -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical "Block3" \ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block3
```

In this example, the top cell of each output database is still TOP. To make the lower-level block the top cell, the -new\_top\_cell command-line option can be used.

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -select_cell_hierarchical \ -new_top_cell TOP,Block1 \ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block1 -vue Block1.vue -vue_template TOP.vue
```

Selection by violation comment and by bounding box is also allowed. For example, to split out only the metal1 rules with no cell selections, the tool might be run as follows

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -svc "M1" \ -o new_pydb/PYDB_TOP_m1 -vue TOP_m1.vue -vue_template TOP.vue
```

However, notice that any heat maps that were at the top level are not copied in this case, since TOP no longer exists in the output database.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Since PYDB does not contain cell placement data, bounding-box selection is valid only within a cell, and there is no looking down the hierarchy. For example, to include top-level data over block1 when the extents of the block1 placement are (100,200),(300,400), the tool might be run this way:

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP \ -select_cell_hierarchical "Block1 \ -select_interacting TOP,100.0,200.0,300.0,400.0 \ -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block1 -vue Block1.vue -vue_template TOP.vue
```

Notice that when error\_options(flatten\_violations) is set, the flattening of violations is allowed to specified blocks during the IC Validator run when the entire hierarchy is available. Using the flatten\_violations argument in conjunction with bounding-box selection allows for geographical partitioning of the errors.

Selection can also be done by error classification using several command-line options to include or exclude errors of certain classifications, and also to drop error classification data from the output.

## Merging Error Databases

The icv\_pydb utility provides the ability to merge multiple error databases (PYDBs) into one, for example, when subblocks or different sets of rules are run separately. In the simple case of merging several PYDBs with the same top cell, the icv\_pydb utility can be run one time for each input database. For example,

```
icv_pydb -i metal1run/run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -o merged_pydb/PYDB_TOP icv_pydb -i metal2run/run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -o merged_pydb/PYDB_TOP ...
```

If merged\_pydb/PYDB\_TOP does not exist, it is created and subsequent runs merge data into the existing database. Alternatively, they might be combined on the command line:

```
icv_pydb -i metal1run/run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP \ -i metal2run/run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP \ -o merged_pydb/PYDB_TOP
```

When merging multiple databases with different top cells, provide a (single instance) translation to the common top cell, so that 'highlight in top cell' works properly in VUE. This can be done using the -new\_top\_cell command-line option. For example,

```
icv_pydb -i block1run/run_details/pydb/PYDB_Block1 \ -new_top_cell Block1,TOP,100,100,0,0 -o merged_pydb/PYDB_TOP icv_pydb -i block2run/run_details/pydb/PYDB_Block2 \ -new_top_cell Block2,TOP,200,100,0,0 -o merged_pydb/PYDB_TOP
```

It is possible that the PYDBs being merged could be at different DBU resolutions. When merging into an existing PYDB, the icv\_pydb tool always uses the DBU of the destination database. However, you can specify a DBU on the command line so that, when creating a new PYDB, the specified DBU is used, and when merging into an existing PYDB, the DBU of the existing database can be verified.

<!-- image -->

The -dbu command-line option allows the DBU to be given as a floating-point value in microns. If merging into an existing database with a different DBU from the value given on the command line, an error is issued and the tool exits.

## Note:

Runset functions are not combined during merging. If two similar runset functions in the same violation are merged, they exist as separate functions in the destination database.

## Applying Waivers to an Existing Error Database

After an IC Validator run, you can apply waivers to an existing PYDB using the error management utility. For example:

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -apply_cell_level_waivers waivers.oas
```

The input waiver database can be in cPYDB or OASIS format. Waivers are matched at the cell level using exact shape matching. You can use the -waiver\_matching\_tolerance argument to set a tolerance. Each waiver shape must exactly overlap the error shape in the same cell for the waiver to apply. This process is sensitive to hierarchy or data cutting changes, which can make error shapes and waiver shapes different.

## VUE File Support

When a new database is created, whether by splitting or merging, you can output a VUE file which points to the new database, by specifying the -vue command-line option. You can also use the corresponding -vue\_template command-line option to specify an input VUE file to be used as a template by replacing only the database name. Otherwise, relevant information is taken from the input PYDB.

## Modifying Databases in Place

Certain operations are supported for modifying a PYDB or cPYDB in place, without a destination database. These are:

```
-rename_cells rename_cells_file -rename_violations rename_violations_file -classify classify.csv
```

<!-- image -->

For modify-in-place operations, only the input PYDB or cPYDB is specified using the -i command-line option. There is no output database.

## Note:

The -classify command-line option is supported only with PYDB and not cPYDB.

## Hierarchy Considerations

The PYDB stores cell descendant information for every unique cell, including an instance translation of all its descendants This enables the splitting of a database to properly update the instance translation to top for 'Highlight In Top Cell' functionality.

A common use model might be to completely split out a subblock and make it the new top cell for the destination PYDB. For example,

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_TOP -o new_pydb/PYDB_Block1 \ -select_cell_hierarchical "Block1" -vue Block1.vue -vue_template \ TOP.vue \ -new_top_cell TOP,Block1
```

In this example hierarchy, a new PYDB is created with Block1 as the top cell and all violations in Block1 and below it are selected. Since PYDB has all of the cell descendant information, a translation is not required when the new top cell is below the original top cell. An error is issued if the new top cell is below the original top cell and cell selection includes anything above the new top cell.

## XML Command File

The XML command file allows any selections available on the command line as well as selection of individual errors by ID. Similar to using command-line options, the XML file can specify multiple source databases and different selections for each. The file can be gzipped.

All standard rules for XML formatting must be followed. Of particular note is that all parameter values must be enclosed in quotation marks, and any special characters such as angle brackets, ampersand, or quotes must be escaped. Example 44 shows the syntax of the XML command file.

## Example 44 XML Command File Syntax

```
<?xml version="1.0"?> <pydb> <pydb_operation> <input_pydb path="run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL"> field_selection_mode="UNION|INTERSECTION">
```

<!-- image -->

```
<select_cell pattern="cellA*"/> <unselect_cell pattern="cellB*"/> <select_cell_hierarchical pattern="cellA*"/> <unselect_cell_hierarchical pattern="cellB*"/> <select_violation_comment pattern="Rule1*"/> <unselect_violation_comment pattern="Rule2*"/> <select_enclosed cell="cellname" x1="1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/> <unselect_enclosed cell="cellname" x1="1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/> <select_interacting cell="cellname" x1="1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/> <unselect_interacting cell="cellname" x1="1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0"\ y2="4.0"/> <select_classified> <class name="Waive"/> ... </select_classified> <unselect_classified> <class name="Waive"/> ... </unselect_classified> <select_layer_names pattern="m1*"/> <unselect_layer_names pattern="m2*"/> <select_layers range="10-11,0-55"/> <unselect_layers range="10-11,0-255"/> <select_explorer_tiers range="<range>"/> <unselect_explorer_tiers range="<range>"/> <rename_cell old="cellA" new="cellB"/> <rename_cells file="rename_cells.csv"/> <rename_violation old="Rule1" new="Rule2"/> <rename_violations file="rename_violations.csv"/> <top_cell old="top1" new="top2" dx="1.0" dy="2.0" angle="90" \ reflected="1" flat_placement_count="1"/> <!-- Select individual errors by ID --> <select_errors command_id="1" cell_id="2"> <error id="1"/> <error id="2"/> ... </select_errors> <!-- No error IDs given == all errors selected --> <select_errors command_id="2" cell_id="2"/> <!-- No error IDs given, no cell ID given == entire command \ selected --> <select_errors command_id="3"/> <!-- Select errors by exact value of a field --> <select_errors field="Instance Name" value="I123"/> <select_errors field="Distance" value="4.5"/> <!-- Select errors by wildcard pattern --> <select_errors field="Instance Name" pattern="I4*"/> <!-- Select errors based on a range of values --> <select_errors field="Distance" min="1.0" max="2.0"/> <!-- Selection conditional on another field for commands like
```

<!-- image -->

```
density --> <select_errors field="Value" min="1.0" max="2.0" when_field="Report" is="Area"/> <!-- Classify errors --> <classify_errors class="Waive" comment="Waive errors in IP block" field_selection_mode="UNION|INTERSECTION"> <!-- Any selection options might go here --> </classify_errors> <exclude_heat_map/> <exclude_error_classification/> </input_pydb> ... <output_pydb path="/path_to_pydb" dbu="0.0001"> <overwrite/> <vue file="output.vue" template="inblock.vue"/> </output_pydb> <output_layout file="output_layout_file" format="GDSII|OASIS"> <violation_map file="mapping_file" out="output_file"/> <include_unmapped/> <input_layout file="input_layout_file" cell="top_cell"/> <command_property number="property_number"/> <host_init host="host1:#cores"/> <host_init host="hostN:#cores"/> </output_layout> </pydb_operation> ... </pydb>
```

## The XML command file syntax is defined as follows:

- &lt;pydb&gt;

Top-level enclosing tag for the command file XML document. There must be one and only one &lt;pydb&gt; tag, as everything else is enclosed in it.

- &lt;pydb\_operation&gt;

Top-level enclosing tag of a single database operation. For example, a split, merge, or copy. There might be multiple pydb\_operation tags in a file.

```
· <input_pydb path="path/to/pydb" field_selection_mode="UNION|INTERSECTION">
```

Designates an input PYDB database, just as the -i command-line option does on the command line. All selections and command-line options within this section apply only to the given input database. If there is no output database specified, the input PYDB can be modified in place. Multiple input databases can be specified for a single pydb\_operation in the XML command file.

The optional field\_selection\_mode attribute controls how &lt;select\_errors&gt; tags based on field values are combined. The default is UNION , which means that errors which meet any &lt;select\_errors field...&gt; criteria is included. If INTERSECTION is specified, then only errors which meet all of the &lt;select\_errors field...&gt; criteria is included.

<!-- image -->

- &lt;select\_layer\_names pattern="m1*"/&gt;

Specifies that only layer names matching a given pattern name (wildcards allowed) are included from this database.

- &lt;unselect\_layer\_names pattern="m2*"/&gt;

Specifies that no layer names matching a given pattern name (wildcards allowed) are included from this database.

- &lt;select\_layers range="10-11,0-255"/&gt;

Specifies that only layers matching the given range are included from this database.

- &lt;unselect\_layers range="10-11,0-255*"/&gt;

Specifies that no layers matching the given range are included from this database.

- &lt;select\_cell pattern="cellA*"/&gt;

Specifies that only cells matching the given pattern (wildcards allowed) are included from this database. Equivalent to the -select\_cell command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;unselect\_cell pattern="cellA*"/&gt;

Specifies that no cells matching the given pattern (wildcards allowed) are included from this database. Equivalent to the -unselect\_cell command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;select\_cell\_hierarchical pattern="cellA*"/&gt;

Specifies that only cells matching the given pattern (wildcards allowed) and their descendants are included from this database. Equivalent to the -select\_cell\_hierarchical command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;unselect\_cell\_hierarchical pattern="cellA*"/&gt;

Specifies that no cells matching the given pattern (wildcards allowed) or their descendants are included from this database. Equivalent to the -unselect\_cell\_hierarchical command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;select\_violation\_comment pattern="cellA*"/&gt;

Specifies that only violation comments matching the given pattern (wildcards allowed) are included from this database. Equivalent to the -svc command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

```
◦ <unselect_violation_comment pattern="cellA*"/>
```

Specifies that no violation comments matching the given pattern (wildcards allowed) are included from this database. Equivalent to the -uvc command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;select\_enclosed cell="cellname" x1="1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/&gt;

Specifies that in the given cell, only errors which are enclosed by the given window coordinates are included. Equivalent to the -select\_enclosed command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;unselect\_enclosed cell="cellname" x1="1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/&gt;

Specifies that in the given cell, no errors which are enclosed by the given window coordinates are included. Equivalent to the -unselect\_enclosed command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

```
◦ <select_interacting cell="cellname" "1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/>
```

Specifies that in the given cell, only errors which interact with the given window coordinates are included. Equivalent to the -select\_interacting command-line option, and can be specified multiple times.

```
◦ <unselect_interacting cell="cellname" "1.0" y1="2.0" x2="3.0" \ y2="4.0"/>
```

Specifies that in the given cell, no errors which interact with the given window coordinates are included. Equivalent to the -unselect\_interacting commandline option, and can be specified multiple times.

```
◦ <select_classified> ... </select_classified>
```

Specifies that only errors that match the given list of classifications are included. Equivalent to the -select\_classified command-line option.

- &lt;unselect\_classified&gt; ... &lt;/unselect\_classified&gt;

Specifies that only errors that match the given list of classifications are included. Equivalent to the -unselect\_classified command-line option.

- &lt;rename\_cell old="cellA" new="cellB"/&gt;

Renames a single cell from this input database. Can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;rename\_cells file="rename\_cells.csv"/&gt;

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Renames cells from this input database according to the given CSV file. Equivalent to the -rename\_cells command-line option.

- &lt;rename\_violation old="Rule1" new="Rule2"/&gt;

Renames a single violation from this input database. Can be specified multiple times.

- &lt;rename\_violations file="rename\_violations.csv"/&gt;

Renames violations from this input database according to the given CSV file. Equivalent to the -rename\_violations command-line option.

```
◦ <top_cell old="top1" new="top2" dx="1.0" dy="2.0" angle="90" \ reflected="1"/>
```

Specifies a different destination top cell than the source database, and provides a translation from the source top cell to the destination top cell. This tag is required if merging into a PYDB with a different top cell. The instance translations to top from the source database are updated to the context of the new top cell to enable highlighting violations in the new top cell.

```
◦ <select_errors command_id="1" cell_id="2"> <error id="1"/> <error id="2"/> ... </select_errors>
```

Selects individual errors to be included from this input PYDB using numeric IDs from the source database. If there are no &lt;error&gt; records within the &lt;select\_errors&gt; record, all errors from the command/cell are included. If the cell\_id is not specified, all errors from the command are included. This tag can be specified multiple times.

```
◦ <select_errors field="Instance Name" value="I123"/> <select_errors field="Distance" value="4.5"/>
```

Specifies that errors where the given string, integer, or double field is equal to the given value are included. The field name should be the heading of the column from the LAYOUT\_ERRORS file. Field-based selection options are combined according to the field\_selection\_mode attribute of the &lt;input\_pydb&gt; or &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section in which they occur.

```
◦ <select_errors field="Instance Name" pattern="I4*"/>
```

Specifies that errors where the given string field matches the given wildcard pattern are included. The field name should be the heading of the column from the LAYOUT\_ERRORS file. Field-based selection options are combined according to the field\_selection\_mode attribute of the &lt;input\_pydb&gt; or &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section in which they occur.

<!-- image -->

```
◦ <select_errors field="Distance" min="1.0" max="2.0"/>
```

Specifies that errors where the given double or integer field is in the given range are included. The field name should be the heading of the column from the LAYOUT\_ERRORS file. Field-based selection options are combined according to the field\_selection\_mode attribute of the &lt;input\_pydb&gt; or &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section in which they occur.

```
◦ <select_errors field="Value" min="1.0" max="2.0" \ when_field="Report" is="Area"/>
```

Specifies that errors which meet the given selection criteria are included. The addition of the when\_field and is attributes make this selection conditional on another value in the row. This is useful for functions such as density() , when there might be many Report and Value pairs for a single error and the selection must be only for a particular Report . The previous example selects density errors with Area in the range of 1.0-2.0. The field name and when\_field should be the headings of the appropriate columns from the LAYOUT\_ERRORS file. Field-based selection options are combined according to the field\_selection\_mode attribute of the &lt;input\_pydb&gt; or &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section in which they occur.

- &lt;classify\_errors class="Waive" comment="Waive errors in IP block" field\_selection\_mode="UNION|INTERSECTION"&gt; &lt;!-- Any selection options might go here --&gt; &lt;/classify\_errors&gt;

Classifies errors in this input PYDB according to the given class and applies the optional user comment. Any error selection options might be specified inside the &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section and combined with selection options that are outside of the &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section. Multiple &lt;classify\_errors&gt; sections can be specified in a single &lt;input\_pydb&gt; section.

The optional field\_selection\_mode attribute controls how &lt;select\_errors&gt; tags based on field values are combined inside this &lt;classify\_errors&gt; section. The default is UNION , which means that errors which meet any &lt;select\_errors field...&gt; criteria are included. If INTERSECTION is specified, then only errors which meet all of the &lt;select\_errors field...&gt; criteria are included.

- &lt;exclude\_heat\_map/&gt;

Specifies that heat map data is not be copied from the input database to the output database. Equivalent to the -exclude\_heat\_map command-line option.

- &lt;exclude\_error\_classification/&gt;

Specifies that error classification data is not be copied from the input database to the output database. Equivalent to the -exclude\_error\_classification command-line option.

- &lt;output\_pydb path="path/to/pydb" dbu="0.0001"&gt;

Designates an output PYDB database, just as the -o command-line option does on the command line. The dbu parameter is optional and is equivalent to the -dbu commandline option. The output\_pydb option can be specified at the most, one time within a single pydb\_operation .

- &lt;overwrite/&gt;

Specifies that if the output database exists, it is overwritten. Otherwise, the data is merged into an existing output database. Equivalent to the -overwrite commandline option.

- &lt;vue file="output.vue" template="inlib.vue"/&gt;

Specifies that the given VUE file should be created which points to the new output database. Equivalent to the -vue command line option. The optional template parameter specifies an existing VUE file to use as a template.

- &lt;output\_layout file="output\_layout\_file" format="GDSII|OASIS"&gt;

Specifies that violations from the input PYDB are exported to the output layout specified by the given file and format.

- &lt;violation\_map file="mapping\_file" out="output\_file"/&gt;

Specifies a violation mapping file or output violation mapping file for this output layout.

- &lt;include\_unmapped/&gt;

If a violation mapping file is used, specifies that violations without an entry in the violation mapping file are included in the output on arbitrarily assigned layers and datatypes.

- &lt;include\_unmapped/&gt;

Specifies the input layout from which the design hierarchy is read.

- &lt;command\_property number="property\_number"/&gt;

Specifies that the runset file:line:function is added to each polygon in the output layout on the given property number. This might increase the size of the output layout substantially.

<!-- image -->

```
◦ <host_init host="host1:#cores"/>
```

Assigns hosts for distributed operations.

## Classifying Errors With the XML Command File

The XML command file provides a way to classify errors using the icv\_pydb tool. Any selection options available for other icv\_pydb operations can also be used to select errors for classification. Example 45 illustrates several common waiver scenarios.

## Example 45 Common Waiver Scenarios

```
<?xml version="1.0"?> <pydb> <pydb_operation> <input_pydb path="run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL" <!-- Waive all the errors for an entire rule --> <classify_errors class="Waive" comment="Waiver for rule M1.R1"> <select_violation_comment pattern="M1.R1*"/> </classify_errors> <!-- Ignore all the errors in particular cells --> <classify_errors class="Ignore" comment="Ignoring errors in IP \ cells"> <select_cell pattern="MYIP*"/> </classify_errors> <!-- Classify errors in a window --> <classify_errors class="Watch" comment="Fix in next rev"> <select_enclosed cell="TOP" x1="0.0" y1="0.0" x2="10.0" \ y2="5.0"/> </classify_errors> <!-- Waive metal1 spacing errors based on Distance --> <classify_errors class="Waive" comment="Waive these"> <select_layer_names pattern="metal1*"/> <select_errors field="Distance" min="1.0" max="2.0"/> </classify_errors> <!-- Waive density errors based on Area --> <classify_errors class="Waive" comment="Accepted density values"> <select_violation_comment pattern="DN*"/> <select_errors field="Value" min="0.0" max="0.5" \ when_field="Report" is="Area"/> </classify_errors> <!-- Waive PERC errors based on combination of device name \ and comment --> <classify_errors class="Waive" comment="Waiving \ M1 path errors" field_selection_mode="UNION">
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
<select_violation_comment pattern="Rule_1*"/> <select_errors field="Device name (Type)" pattern="*/M1 *"/> <select_errors field="Comment" pattern="Gate has \ no path to power, ground, or top-level port"/> </classify_errors> <!-- Waive PERC errors with certain instance names --> <classify_errors class="Waive" comment="Waiving specific \ instances"> <select_violation_comment pattern="Rule_2*"/> <!-- The default field_selection_mode is "UNION"--> <select_errors field="Reference Instance (Cell Name)" \ pattern="XI123 *"/> <select_errors field="Reference Instance (Cell Name)" pattern="XI456 *"/> </classify_errors> </input_pydb> </pydb_operation> </pydb>
```

## Exporting Errors to a Layout

The icv\_pydb utility provides the capability to export errors from one or more error databases (PYDBs) to a GDSII or OASIS layout file. All selection options that the icv\_pydb utility provides are supported. The design hierarchy must be read from the original input layout, which was used for the IC Validator run. Layer and datatype numbers might be specified by a violation mapping file, or they are assigned arbitrarily.

The violation mapping file is a CSV file with the following columns:

- Violation comment

Required. The full text of the violation or rule comment. Wildcard matching is supported.

- Command

Optional. The runset file:line:function of a specific IC Validator command within the given rule. Wildcard matching is supported. If this column is empty, all commands within the violation or rule is matched.

- Layer

Required. The layer number that is used to output matching violations.

- Datatype

Required. The datatype number that is used to output matching violations.

<!-- image -->

If a violation map file is given, only the rules and commands listed in the violation mapping file are exported. To include rules and commands without a listing in the violation map file, use the -include\_unmapped command-line option.

If no input layout is given, the icv\_pydb utility attempts to use the original layout path stored with the PYDB to read the design hierarchy.

## Example 46 Example of Exporting to OASIS

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL \ -o errors.oas -format OASIS -layout AD4FUL.GDS -c AD4FUL \ -violation_map violation_map.csv
```

Example 47 Example With Selections and Creating a Reference Violation Mapping File With the Layers and Datatypes Used

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL \ -svc "Met1*" -select_cell "AD4FUL" \ -o errors.oas -format OASIS \ -violation_map_output violation_map_used.csv
```

Example 48 Example of Creating a Violation Map File With Arbitrarily Assigned Layer and Datatype Numbers From a PYDB

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL \ -violation_map_output violation_map.csv
```

## Managing Referenced cPYDB Paths

When an error classification database (cPYDB) is used to apply error classifications during an IC Validator run, the error database (PYDB) contains a link to the cPYDB. Some details such as classification comments and timestamps are not stored in the PYDB but are read from the referenced cPYDB by tools such as VUE when needed. If the cPYDB is not in the original location, these details might be missing. The icv\_pydb utility provides the capability to edit the path to referenced cPYDBs so that VUE can load those classification details.

## Example 49 Example of Listing the cPYDBs Referenced by a PYDB

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL -list_cpydbs ... cPYDBs referenced by run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL: Path: /global/cpydb1 Name: CPYDB1 Path: /global/cpydb1 Name: CPYDB1A
```

```
Path: /global/cpydb2 Name: CPYDB2
```

## Example 50 Example of Updating the cPYDB Paths Using the -rename\_cpydb\_paths Command-Line Option

```
icv_pydb -i run_details/pydb/PYDB_AD4FUL -rename_cpydb_paths "*cpydb1" "/new/path/cpydb1" \ -rename_cpydb_paths "*cpydb2" "/new_path/cpydb2" ... Renamed cPYDBs: Old Path: /global/cpydb1 New Path: /new/path/cpydb1 Name: CPYDB1 Old Path: /global/cpydb1 New Path: /new/path/cpydb1 Name: CPYDB1A Old Path: /global/cpydb2 New Path: /new/path/cpydb2 Name: CPYDB2
```
